<p class="theme-lead">Real-world systems change constantly: jobs arrive, machines break down, demands and travel times are uncertain. Re-optimising after every change is too slow. My research uses <b>genetic programming (GP)</b> to automatically learn <b>decision rules</b> that make high-quality decisions <b>in real time</b> — in microseconds, with formulas people can read.</p>

<a name="introduction"></a>
<h2>Introduction</h2>
<h3>Decisions that cannot wait</h3>
<p>In a dynamic job shop, every time a machine becomes idle it must choose which waiting job to process next; in uncertain arc routing, a vehicle must choose its next street when it finishes a task. These decisions must be made immediately, using only the current state.</p>

<div class="theme-split__text">
<h3>Why genetic programming?</h3>
<ul>
<li><b>Learns the rule itself</b> — GP searches over programs, discovering new rule structures rather than tuning parameters.</li>
<li><b>Fast at decision time</b> — evaluating a formula takes microseconds.</li>
<li><b>Readable</b> — experts can inspect and trust the evolved rule.</li>
<li><b>Trained in simulation</b> — learned offline on many scenarios, reused online.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

<a name="contributions"></a>
<h2>My Contributions</h2>
<p>With my students and collaborators, I have made the following contributions. Click a title to read the paper, or <i>list entry</i> to see it in my publication list.</p>

<h3 class="theme-sub"><span class="theme-sub__num">1</span> Scheduling heuristics for dynamic job shops</h3>
<p>Our core line of work makes GP hyper-heuristics effective for dynamic (flexible) job shop scheduling: evolving routing and sequencing rules together, selecting the most useful features, and combining rules into ensembles. It is summarised in our Springer book and surveys.</p>

<h3 class="theme-sub"><span class="theme-sub__num">2</span> Routing policies under uncertainty</h3>
<p>For arc and vehicle routing with uncertain demands and costs, we evolve routing policies that let each vehicle decide its next task on the fly, including vehicle collaboration, niching and multi-objective trade-offs.</p>

<h3 class="theme-sub"><span class="theme-sub__num">3</span> New program representations</h3>
<p>We introduced linear and grammar-guided linear GP to scheduling, enabling rules with reusable sub-expressions and flow-control logic.</p>

<h3 class="theme-sub"><span class="theme-sub__num">4</span> Learning faster with surrogates</h3>
<p>Evaluating a rule needs many simulations. Our surrogate models and multi-fidelity evaluation estimate rule quality cheaply, cutting training time substantially.</p>
